releases.title: desktop/26 latest desktop-variant snap
releases.body: Rolling latest desktop-variant core26-desktop build from desktop/26; assets are replaced on every green build. Consumed by ubuntu-core-desktop’s image CI. (Until 2026-11-23 this release was called desktop-26-thin-latest, a name kept from the 2026-11-09 branch rename so it could not clobber the fat branch’s desktop-26-latest release.)

releases.title: Ubuntu Core Desktop 26 KDE (dangerous) - 20261127
releases.body: Rolling developer preview, replaced by every green build on desktop/26. Signed with an individual’s registered test key; snaps are unasserted and can never be refreshed. No credentials are baked in: first boot runs the plasma-setup first-boot wizard (the KDE equivalent of GNOME’s ubuntu-desktop-init) to create the user account. See manifest.txt for the source commit and the snap versions in this image. If the image was split into *.img.zst.partNN files (GitHub’s 2GiB asset cap), reassemble first: cat ubuntu-core-desktop-kde.img.zst.part* > ubuntu-core-desktop-kde.img.zst, then verify against SHA256SUMS. Decompress with: zstd -T0 -d --sparse ubuntu-core-desktop-kde.img.zst -o pc.img (the –sparse flag is required or the output allocates the full ~20G). Boot with virt-install or qemu per README.md.

releases.title: Myna 0.3.3
releases.body:
Highlights

  • Hindi dictation. A new model, IndicConformer (AI4Bharat), installs as the myna-indicconformer snap, and Myna Settings recommends it for Hindi and sets it up on a Hindi desktop. On the FLEURS Hindi test set it writes 12% of words wrong, against 31% for Whisper large-v3-turbo on a GPU, the best Myna offered for Hindi until now, and it runs on the CPU, finishing about 0.15 s after you stop speaking (#82).
  • Text that Myna could not type, because focus left the field while it was still finishing, is now reported as lost instead of disappearing silently.
  • Fixes in how Myna types through IBus, including a memory bug in the preedit text it shows while you speak (#18).
  • New Azerbaijani translation; updates to Esperanto, French and Simplified Chinese.
  • Myna Settings from the retired ppa:charles05/myna-config now gets updates again: upgrading moves the system to ppa:canonical-desktop-team/myna (#111).

Thanks

  • anilsapkota, for the Hindi evaluation that made the case for IndicConformer (#82).

For the translation work,

  • On Hosted Weblate: David D. (French), Nicat (Azerbaijani), Nova_Chen (Simplified Chinese) and phlostically (Esperanto).

Install

On Ubuntu 24.04 LTS or later, install Myna Settings from the PPA:

sudo add-apt-repository ppa:canonical-desktop-team/myna
sudo apt install myna-config

Myna Settings then sets up the rest: the Dictation app and a speech model. They come from the Snap Store’s latest/edge channel as myna, myna-parakeet, myna-whisper, myna-funasr and myna-nemotron.

Myna works on GNOME, Xfce and KDE Plasma 6.

arm64 is experimental: the speech models run on the CPU, and Parakeet’s NVIDIA GPU engine is built for arm64 but has not been tried on hardware yet.

releases.title: Myna 0.3.2
releases.body:
Highlights

  • Vocabulary now works with every model. Whisper and FunASR join Parakeet in writing your names and terms the way you typed them, and each correction is checked against the audio first, so ordinary words stay as spoken. The word list moved to Myna Settings’ General tab (#1). The check has a cost on Whisper: with 100 words in the list, Whisper small takes about 0.44 s longer (median) to finish a phrase, 0.16 s with 10 words.
  • Parakeet transcribes faster: a 0.3.1 bug re-ran the decode over and over when the vocabulary was empty, making it 2.7x slower on average and more on long phrases.
  • Myna Settings’ Diagnostics shows how noisy your last dictation was (signal-to-noise ratio), and the background-noise warning now looks at that instead of at loudness, so a hot mic such as AirPods no longer trips it on clean speech, and real babble now does.
  • Holding the dictation key no longer starts a second dictation right after the first one ends.
  • In an app Myna cannot type into, such as the VSCodium snap, Myna now says “No text field focused” instead of starting and stopping a second later (#91).
  • Setting up Myna retries once when the Snap Store times out, instead of reporting that Myna failed.
  • New translations: Swedish, Hungarian and Simplified Chinese; updates to Esperanto, Estonian, French and Slovak.

Thanks

For the translation work,

  • On Hosted Weblate: Balázs Úr (Hungarian), Daniel Nylander (Swedish), David D. (French), Nova_Chen and tianhe-team (Simplified Chinese), Peter Vančo (Slovak), phlostically (Esperanto) and Priit Jõerüüt (Estonian).

Install

On Ubuntu 24.04 LTS or later, install Myna Settings from the PPA:

sudo add-apt-repository ppa:canonical-desktop-team/myna
sudo apt install myna-config

Myna Settings then sets up the rest: the Dictation app and a speech model. They come from the Snap Store’s latest/edge channel as myna, myna-parakeet, myna-whisper, myna-funasr and myna-nemotron.

Myna works on GNOME, Xfce and KDE Plasma 6.

arm64 is experimental: the speech models run on the CPU, and Parakeet’s NVIDIA GPU engine is built for arm64 but has not been tried on hardware yet.

releases.title: Myna 0.3.1
releases.body:
Highlights

  • Teach Myna your words. Add names and terms to the vocabulary in Myna Settings’ Model tab, and the Parakeet model listens for them: a word it used to misspell, or split (“pulse audio” for PulseAudio), is far more likely to come out the way you wrote it (#1).
  • Whisper and FunASR do not use the vocabulary yet, and its row is hidden while one of them is the active model.
  • Switching engine or model no longer leaves the old one’s files on disk (#61).
  • Typing on Plasma Wayland keeps your keyboard layout during a dictation (#4).
  • Setting up Myna on Xfce and Plasma no longer stops at the indicator step until the next login (#79).
  • On Plasma with software rendering, the first dictation no longer stalls while the pill starts.

Known issues

  • A word that sounds exactly like a common one can still come out as the common word: “Myna” is heard as “minor” or “miner” in some accents.
  • Upgrading waits for your next logout: the running pill holds back the snap refresh (#38). The fix is waiting on the Snap Store.

Install

On Ubuntu 24.04 LTS or later, install Myna Settings from the PPA:

sudo add-apt-repository ppa:canonical-desktop-team/myna
sudo apt install myna-config

Myna Settings then sets up the rest: the Dictation app and a speech model. They come from the Snap Store’s latest/edge channel as myna, myna-parakeet, myna-whisper and myna-funasr.

Myna works on GNOME, Xfce and KDE Plasma 6.

arm64 is experimental: the speech models run on the CPU, and Parakeet’s NVIDIA GPU engine is built for arm64 but has not been tried on hardware yet.

commits.message:
e2e: Log page state when the browser login times out (#2216)

When the e2e browser login times out, the log does not show what the
page displayed. A wrong page, a slow load, and an unexpected UI change
all look the same.

On every `wait_for_pattern` timeout, log the page URI, title, load
progress, and the full visible text. The full text is logged because the
useful message can sit lower on the page.

The helper runs only on failure and swallows its own errors, so the
timeout result does not change.

Validated with a forced timeout in a GTK/WebKit window under Xvfb: the
log line prints with the full text, and the success path is unchanged.

commits.author: Robert Ancell
commits.message:
ci: automate releases and publishing to pub.dev (#413)

## Summary

Automates releases and publishing to pub.dev from GitHub Actions,
replacing the manual `chore: release` commit + `dart pub publish` flow.

### Flow

1. Conventional commits land on `main`.
2. `release.yml` (release-please) opens/updates a `chore: release X.Y.Z`
PR that bumps `pubspec.yaml` and `CHANGELOG.md`.
3. Merging that PR creates the `vX.Y.Z` tag + GitHub release, then
dispatches `publish.yml` on the tag (tags created with `GITHUB_TOKEN`
don't trigger `push` workflows).
4. `publish.yml` verifies the tag matches `pubspec.yaml`, runs analyze +
tests, then publishes via `dart-lang/setup-dart`'s reusable workflow
using OIDC (no secrets). It also runs on a manually pushed `vX.Y.Z` tag.

### Changes

- `.github/workflows/release.yml`: release-please + dispatch of publish.
- `.github/workflows/publish.yml`: verify + publish (`push` tags and
`workflow_dispatch`).
- `.github/workflows/publish-dry-run.yml`: `dart pub publish --dry-run`
on PRs.
- `.github/workflows/semantic-pr.yml`: enforces conventional PR titles.
- `release-please-config.json` / `.release-please-manifest.json`: `dart`
release type, `v` tags, pre-1.0 `feat` -> patch bump, bootstrapped at
`0.8.1` so the next release only includes new commits.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: documents the release process.

Resolves UDENG-12242

commits.author: Adrian Dombeck
commits.message:
Preserve non-ASCII copyright holders

The generator relied on Python's locale when decoding licensecheck
output.  A non-UTF-8 locale could turn UTF-8 names into mojibake in
debian/copyright. Decode the machine-readable output as UTF-8
explicitly.

commits.author: Kat
commits.message:
feat(gh-actions/go): New action to bump toolchain patch version (#150)

Added a new composite GH action to open PRs and update Go toolchain
directive patch versions. This works with both `go.work` and `go.mod`
files.

Generally, we want to always use the latest Go toolchain patch version
where possible, as security fixes are often tied to it. This new action
aims to simplify this process by scanning for places where the toolchain
directive is used, and open PRs to update the patch version to the
latest version when needed.

Note: we **only touch the patch version**.

By default, we ignore files in `*/vendor/*`, `*/testdata/*`, and
`*/.git/*` based on `find`'s parsing/searching.

commits.author: kkuo
commits.message:
feat(gh-actions/go): New action to bump toolchain patch version

Added a new composite GH action to open PRs and update Go toolchain directive patch versions. This works with both `go.work` and `go.mod` files.

Generally, we want to always use the latest Go toolchain patch version where possible as security fixes are often tied to it. This new action aims to simplify this process by scanning for places where the toolchain directive is used, and open PRs to update the patch version to the latest version when needed.

Note, we only ever touch the patch version.

By default, we ignore files in `*/vendor/*`, `*/testdata/*`, and `*/.git/*` based on `find`'s, parsing/searching.

commits.message:
ci: automate releases and publishing to pub.dev (#47)

## Summary

Automates releases and publishing to pub.dev from GitHub Actions,
replacing the manual `chore: release` commit + `dart pub publish` flow.

### Flow

1. Conventional commits land on `main`.
2. `release.yml` (release-please) opens/updates a `chore: release X.Y.Z`
PR that bumps `pubspec.yaml` and `CHANGELOG.md`.
3. Merging that PR creates the `vX.Y.Z` tag + GitHub release, then
dispatches `publish.yml` on the tag (tags created with `GITHUB_TOKEN`
don't trigger `push` workflows).
4. `publish.yml` verifies the tag matches `pubspec.yaml`, runs analyze +
tests, then publishes via `dart-lang/setup-dart`'s reusable workflow
using OIDC (no secrets). It also runs on a manually pushed `vX.Y.Z` tag.

### Changes

- `.github/workflows/release.yml`: release-please + dispatch of publish.
- `.github/workflows/publish.yml`: verify + publish (`push` tags and
`workflow_dispatch`).
- `.github/workflows/publish-dry-run.yml`: `dart pub publish --dry-run`
on PRs.
- `.github/workflows/semantic-pr.yml`: enforces conventional PR titles.
- `release-please-config.json` / `.release-please-manifest.json`: `dart`
release type, `v` tags, pre-1.0 `feat` -> patch bump, bootstrapped at
`0.6.3` so the next release only includes new commits.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: documents the release process.

Resolves UDENG-12251

commits.author: Robert Ancell
commits.message:
ci: automate releases and publishing to pub.dev (#26)

## Summary

Automates releases and publishing to pub.dev from GitHub Actions,
replacing the manual `chore: release` commit + `dart pub publish` flow.

### Flow

1. Conventional commits land on `main`.
2. `release.yml` (release-please) opens/updates a `chore: release X.Y.Z`
PR that bumps `pubspec.yaml` and `CHANGELOG.md`.
3. Merging that PR creates the `vX.Y.Z` tag + GitHub release, then
dispatches `publish.yml` on the tag (tags created with `GITHUB_TOKEN`
don't trigger `push` workflows).
4. `publish.yml` verifies the tag matches `pubspec.yaml`, runs analyze +
tests, then publishes via `dart-lang/setup-dart`'s reusable workflow
using OIDC (no secrets). It also runs on a manually pushed `vX.Y.Z` tag.

### Changes

- `.github/workflows/release.yml`: release-please + dispatch of publish.
- `.github/workflows/publish.yml`: verify + publish (`push` tags and
`workflow_dispatch`).
- `.github/workflows/publish-dry-run.yml`: `dart pub publish --dry-run`
on PRs.
- `.github/workflows/semantic-pr.yml`: enforces conventional PR titles.
- `release-please-config.json` / `.release-please-manifest.json`: `dart`
release type, `v` tags, pre-1.0 `feat` -> patch bump, bootstrapped at
`0.5.0` so the next release only includes new commits.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: documents the release process.


Resolves UDENG-12256

Changelog

Sourced from github.com/jackc/pgx/v5's changelog.

5.13.0 (November 11, 2026)

This release adds automatic client certificate reloading and temporal precision metadata for database/sql. It also fixes a panic on malformed server responses, unsafe retries after connection failures, and range encoding. See Changes for client certificate configuration behavior that may affect existing applications.

Security Fixes

  • Panic in Rows.Values on malformed server responses (GHSA-w9rp-vfrh-q8vv). A server response containing fewer row values than declared fields could cause an index-out-of-range panic in Rows.Values. It now returns an error and closes the rows when the counts differ, including when there are extra values, matching Rows.Scan validation.

Features

  • pgconn: reload client certificates and keys configured through sslcert and sslkey for each TLS certificate request, allowing new connections to pick up rotated credentials without recreating the configuration or restarting the application. Files are still validated during configuration parsing. Relative paths retain their parse-time directory, and reloads follow symlinks (Erin Shepherd)
  • stdlib: expose fractional seconds precision for timestamp, timestamptz, time, timetz, and interval through ColumnTypePrecisionScale and database/sql.ColumnType.DecimalSize. These return precision 0, the fractional seconds precision as scale, and ok=true. The scale defaults to 6 when no fractional seconds precision is declared; precision 0 means numeric precision is not applicable (Danny Xu)

Changes

  • pgconn: file-backed client certificates are no longer stored in the parsed TLSConfig.Certificates slice. Setting TLSConfig.Certificates (including a non-nil empty slice) or TLSConfig.GetClientCertificate overrides automatic reloading. Replacing TLSConfig, including with a direct TLSConfig.Clone, discards the file-backed certificate settings; use pgconn.Config.Copy to preserve them when copying a configuration. Certificate and key files must remain readable for subsequent TLS certificate requests. Encrypted keys reuse the password resolved during configuration parsing; GetSSLPassword is not called again on reload.

Bug Fixes

  • pgconn: do not mark a connection-closed error encountered while receiving a response as safe to retry, since the request may already have reached the server. This prevents database/sql from automatically repeating a statement that may already have executed. The error still supports errors.Is(err, pgconn.ErrConnClosed) (Aayush Shah)
  • pgconn: skip sending a cancel request when a connection fails during startup, avoiding an unnecessary second connection attempt (felipe stival)
  • pgconn: accept unencrypted combined certificate/key PEM files with the certificate before the key, as well as key-first files (Erin Shepherd)
  • pgtype: encode Range[any] values returned by RangeCodec.DecodeValue and Rows.Values in both binary and text formats, allowing decoded ranges and multiranges to be reused as query arguments or in CopyFrom (waw666waw666)
  • stdlib: report ok=false for the precision and scale of unconstrained numeric columns instead of bogus values (Danny Xu)
  • stdlib: report math.MaxInt64 for the lengths of unconstrained varchar, bpchar, and varbit columns instead of negative lengths (PerryLink)

Updates `github.com/pressly/goose/v3` from 3.29.0 to 3.30.1
Release notes

Sourced from github.com/pressly/goose/v3's releases.

v3.30.1

Changed

  • +goose ENVSUB ON: support more shell expansions, such as ${VAR:?message}, ${VAR:+word}, and ${#VAR}. A $ that does not start a variable name, such as $1, is now kept as-is instead of an error (#1174)

Fixed

  • Build failure when github.com/mfridman/interpolate is upgraded to v0.2.0, for example with go get -u (#1176)
  • Lock: fix an edge case where a long-lived locker could stop waiting for a held lock and fail immediately. Programs that migrate once at startup were not affected (#1173)

v3.30.0

Added

  • Container image at ghcr.io/pressly/goose for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, published on each release. The image is based on distroless static, runs as a nonroot user, and supports .sql migrations only (#1093)

Changed

  • Various dependency upgrades
  • SQL parser: reduce memory use when parsing migration files, and make parsing much faster when the race detector is on (#1155, #1156)

Fixed

  • CLI: goose validate failed on Go migrations that register an inlined function (#1110)
  • Provider: SQL-only migrations with unpadded versions (1_, 2_, 10_) were sorted by filename instead of version. This affected ListSources and GetVersions, as well as Up when versioning was disabled (#1124)

Updates `github.com/testcontainers/testcontainers-go` from 0.44.0 to 0.45.0
Release notes

Sourced from github.com/testcontainers/testcontainers-go's releases.

v0.45.0

What's Changed

⚠️ Breaking Changes

  • chore(modules)!: extract CockroachDB and Dex client adapters (#4087) @​mdelapenya

Client SDK dependencies have moved into separate examples modules. For CockroachDB, ConnectionConfig is now available through cockroachdbexamples.NewContainer(c) in modules/cockroachdb/examples. The parent’s ConnectionString and MustConnectionString now return PostgreSQL URLs instead of registered pgx handles, and importing the parent no longer registers the pgx SQL driver. Use the examples adapter to retain the previous SDK behavior, or configure the driver yourself.

For Dex, AddClient, RemoveClient, AddUser, and RemoveUser have moved from *dex.Container to dexexamples.NewAdminClient(c) in modules/dex/examples. Static configuration through WithClient and WithUser is unchanged.

  • chore(modules)!: isolate client examples across ten modules (#4081) @​mdelapenya

For Cosmos DB, ContainerPolicy and NewContainerPolicy have moved from modules/azure/cosmosdb to modules/azure/examples/cosmosdb. Update the adapter import; its constructor still accepts the parent container. Run, Container, and ConnectionString remain unchanged in the parent module.

🔒 Security

releases.title: Ubuntu22.04LTS/2204.1.22
releases.body:
Issues / bug reports

  • Addressed crashes on the slide show application reported by the store insights (#199) by better handling exit requests (https://github.com/ubuntu/ubuntu-wsl-splash/pull/25)
  • Enabled collecting debug symbols of all compiled binaries as release assets for future crash analysis (#263, #261, #260, https://github.com/ubuntu/ubuntu-wsl-splash/pull/27 and #1036)
  • Added more languages to the slide show (https://github.com/ubuntu/ubuntu-wsl-splash/pull/18, https://github.com/ubuntu/ubuntu-wsl-splash/pull/21, https://github.com/ubuntu/ubuntu-wsl-splash/pull/23 and https://github.com/ubuntu/ubuntu-wsl-splash/pull/24)

Other enhancements

  • Updated rootfs image to Ubuntu 22.04.1.
  • Implemented a patch for the release upgrader policy (#239 and #264)
  • Updated the store listing to point to the correct Ubuntu WSL website (#247)

What’s Changed

Other enhancements are mostly relevant to the Ubuntu Preview app, which is not directly related to this release.

  • Added check around optional splash access by @EduardGomezEscandell in https://github.com/ubuntu/WSL/pull/207
  • Fix no-return lambda warning by @EduardGomezEscandell in https://github.com/ubuntu/WSL/pull/209
  • Enable launcher command after exiting by @EduardGomezEscandell in https://github.com/ubuntu/WSL/pull/210
  • QA is cancelled when a new commit is pushed by @EduardGomezEscandell in https://github.com/ubuntu/WSL/pull/215
  • Bump runner version for the Jira sync workflow by @GabrielNagy in https://github.com/ubuntu/WSL/pull/216
  • This app rootdir by @CarlosNihelton in https://github.com/ubuntu/WSL/pull/220
  • Prevents running the build workflow on draft PRs by @CarlosNihelton in https://github.com/ubuntu/WSL/pull/219
  • Enables checking if localhost forwarding is disabled by @CarlosNihelton in https://github.com/ubuntu/WSL/pull/218
  • Created class to deal with interprocess syncronization by @EduardGomezEscandell in https://github.com/ubuntu/WSL/pull/221
  • Solved some clang-tidy complaints by @EduardGomezEscandell in https://github.com/ubuntu/WSL/pull/224
  • Better testing proposal by @EduardGomezEscandell in https://github.com/ubuntu/WSL/pull/222
  • Refresh releases and assets by @github-actions in https://github.com/ubuntu/WSL/pull/227
  • Enables MSBuild to update and build the Flutter app if required by @CarlosNihelton in https://github.com/ubuntu/WSL/pull/229
  • Created class to temporarily set root as Ubuntu WSL user safely by @EduardGomezEscandell in https://github.com/ubuntu/WSL/pull/223
  • Extracts the process handling out of the splash controller by @CarlosNihelton in https://github.com/ubuntu/WSL/pull/233
  • Enables downloading images from the c-i.u.c/wsl by @CarlosNihelton in https://github.com/ubuntu/WSL/pull/235
  • Skip C++ source linting for unrelevant PRs by @CarlosNihelton in https://github.com/ubuntu/WSL/pull/236
  • Refresh releases and assets by @github-actions in https://github.com/ubuntu/WSL/pull/230
  • Prevents filesystem exceptions by @CarlosNihelton in https://github.com/ubuntu/WSL/pull/237
  • Adapts the image base name to the new pipeline by @CarlosNihelton in https://github.com/ubuntu/WSL/pull/238
  • Removed Sudo::WslLaunch by @EduardGomezEscandell in https://github.com/ubuntu/WSL/pull/240
  • showConsoleWindow accepts topWindow nullptr by @CarlosNihelton in https://github.com/ubuntu/WSL/pull/243
  • [CI] Sets a 20 min timeout for clang-tidy by @CarlosNihelton in https://github.com/ubuntu/WSL/pull/245

commits.author: Carlos Nihelton
commits.message:
Deploys a systemd environment generator (#61)

[systemd-envirnoment-generator](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.environment-generator.html)

It exposes key environment variables to all systemd units:
  - WSL2_DISTRO_NAME = the instance name
- WSL2_USER_PROFILE = The Windows absolute path of the user profile
directory (e.g. C:\Users\username)

Before this change:

```text
u@DESKTOP-551PQ9O:/mnt/c/Users/User$ systemctl show-environment
LANG=C.UTF-8
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/snap/bin
```

After:

```text
u@DESKTOP-551PQ9O:/mnt/c/Users/User$ systemctl show-environment
LANG=C.UTF-8
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/snap/bin
WSL2_DISTRO_NAME=Ubuntu-26.10
WSL2_USER_PROFILE=C:/Users/User
```

All systemd units inherit those variables by default, and the generator
runs quite early, so cloud-init and wsl-pro-service are some examples of
units that can benefit from this to simplify their implementation.

commits.message:
e2e: Log page state when the browser login times out (#2216)

When the e2e browser login times out, the log does not show what the
page displayed. A wrong page, a slow load, and an unexpected UI change
all look the same.

On every `wait_for_pattern` timeout, log the page URI, title, load
progress, and the full visible text. The full text is logged because the
useful message can sit lower on the page.

The helper runs only on failure and swallows its own errors, so the
timeout result does not change.

Validated with a forced timeout in a GTK/WebKit window under Xvfb: the
log line prints with the full text, and the success path is unchanged.

commits.author: Robert Ancell
commits.message:
ci: automate releases and publishing to pub.dev (#413)

## Summary

Automates releases and publishing to pub.dev from GitHub Actions,
replacing the manual `chore: release` commit + `dart pub publish` flow.

### Flow

1. Conventional commits land on `main`.
2. `release.yml` (release-please) opens/updates a `chore: release X.Y.Z`
PR that bumps `pubspec.yaml` and `CHANGELOG.md`.
3. Merging that PR creates the `vX.Y.Z` tag + GitHub release, then
dispatches `publish.yml` on the tag (tags created with `GITHUB_TOKEN`
don't trigger `push` workflows).
4. `publish.yml` verifies the tag matches `pubspec.yaml`, runs analyze +
tests, then publishes via `dart-lang/setup-dart`'s reusable workflow
using OIDC (no secrets). It also runs on a manually pushed `vX.Y.Z` tag.

### Changes

- `.github/workflows/release.yml`: release-please + dispatch of publish.
- `.github/workflows/publish.yml`: verify + publish (`push` tags and
`workflow_dispatch`).
- `.github/workflows/publish-dry-run.yml`: `dart pub publish --dry-run`
on PRs.
- `.github/workflows/semantic-pr.yml`: enforces conventional PR titles.
- `release-please-config.json` / `.release-please-manifest.json`: `dart`
release type, `v` tags, pre-1.0 `feat` -> patch bump, bootstrapped at
`0.8.1` so the next release only includes new commits.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: documents the release process.

Resolves UDENG-12242

commits.message:
feat(gh-actions/go): New action to bump toolchain patch version (#150)

Added a new composite GH action to open PRs and update Go toolchain
directive patch versions. This works with both `go.work` and `go.mod`
files.

Generally, we want to always use the latest Go toolchain patch version
where possible, as security fixes are often tied to it. This new action
aims to simplify this process by scanning for places where the toolchain
directive is used, and open PRs to update the patch version to the
latest version when needed.

Note: we **only touch the patch version**.

By default, we ignore files in `*/vendor/*`, `*/testdata/*`, and
`*/.git/*` based on `find`'s parsing/searching.

commits.author: kkuo
commits.message:
feat(gh-actions/go): New action to bump toolchain patch version

Added a new composite GH action to open PRs and update Go toolchain directive patch versions. This works with both `go.work` and `go.mod` files.

Generally, we want to always use the latest Go toolchain patch version where possible as security fixes are often tied to it. This new action aims to simplify this process by scanning for places where the toolchain directive is used, and open PRs to update the patch version to the latest version when needed.

Note, we only ever touch the patch version.

By default, we ignore files in `*/vendor/*`, `*/testdata/*`, and `*/.git/*` based on `find`'s, parsing/searching.

commits.author: Robert Ancell
commits.message:
ci: automate releases and publishing to pub.dev (#47)

## Summary

Automates releases and publishing to pub.dev from GitHub Actions,
replacing the manual `chore: release` commit + `dart pub publish` flow.

### Flow

1. Conventional commits land on `main`.
2. `release.yml` (release-please) opens/updates a `chore: release X.Y.Z`
PR that bumps `pubspec.yaml` and `CHANGELOG.md`.
3. Merging that PR creates the `vX.Y.Z` tag + GitHub release, then
dispatches `publish.yml` on the tag (tags created with `GITHUB_TOKEN`
don't trigger `push` workflows).
4. `publish.yml` verifies the tag matches `pubspec.yaml`, runs analyze +
tests, then publishes via `dart-lang/setup-dart`'s reusable workflow
using OIDC (no secrets). It also runs on a manually pushed `vX.Y.Z` tag.

### Changes

- `.github/workflows/release.yml`: release-please + dispatch of publish.
- `.github/workflows/publish.yml`: verify + publish (`push` tags and
`workflow_dispatch`).
- `.github/workflows/publish-dry-run.yml`: `dart pub publish --dry-run`
on PRs.
- `.github/workflows/semantic-pr.yml`: enforces conventional PR titles.
- `release-please-config.json` / `.release-please-manifest.json`: `dart`
release type, `v` tags, pre-1.0 `feat` -> patch bump, bootstrapped at
`0.6.3` so the next release only includes new commits.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: documents the release process.

Resolves UDENG-12251

releases.title: Myna 0.3.3
releases.body:
Highlights

  • Hindi dictation. A new model, IndicConformer (AI4Bharat), installs as the myna-indicconformer snap, and Myna Settings recommends it for Hindi and sets it up on a Hindi desktop. On the FLEURS Hindi test set it writes 12% of words wrong, against 31% for Whisper large-v3-turbo on a GPU, the best Myna offered for Hindi until now, and it runs on the CPU, finishing about 0.15 s after you stop speaking (#82).
  • Text that Myna could not type, because focus left the field while it was still finishing, is now reported as lost instead of disappearing silently.
  • Fixes in how Myna types through IBus, including a memory bug in the preedit text it shows while you speak (#18).
  • New Azerbaijani translation; updates to Esperanto, French and Simplified Chinese.
  • Myna Settings from the retired ppa:charles05/myna-config now gets updates again: upgrading moves the system to ppa:canonical-desktop-team/myna (#111).

Thanks

  • anilsapkota, for the Hindi evaluation that made the case for IndicConformer (#82).

For the translation work,

  • On Hosted Weblate: David D. (French), Nicat (Azerbaijani), Nova_Chen (Simplified Chinese) and phlostically (Esperanto).

Install

On Ubuntu 24.04 LTS or later, install Myna Settings from the PPA:

sudo add-apt-repository ppa:canonical-desktop-team/myna
sudo apt install myna-config

Myna Settings then sets up the rest: the Dictation app and a speech model. They come from the Snap Store’s latest/edge channel as myna, myna-parakeet, myna-whisper, myna-funasr and myna-nemotron.

Myna works on GNOME, Xfce and KDE Plasma 6.

arm64 is experimental: the speech models run on the CPU, and Parakeet’s NVIDIA GPU engine is built for arm64 but has not been tried on hardware yet.

releases.title: Myna 0.3.2
releases.body:
Highlights

  • Vocabulary now works with every model. Whisper and FunASR join Parakeet in writing your names and terms the way you typed them, and each correction is checked against the audio first, so ordinary words stay as spoken. The word list moved to Myna Settings’ General tab (#1). The check has a cost on Whisper: with 100 words in the list, Whisper small takes about 0.44 s longer (median) to finish a phrase, 0.16 s with 10 words.
  • Parakeet transcribes faster: a 0.3.1 bug re-ran the decode over and over when the vocabulary was empty, making it 2.7x slower on average and more on long phrases.
  • Myna Settings’ Diagnostics shows how noisy your last dictation was (signal-to-noise ratio), and the background-noise warning now looks at that instead of at loudness, so a hot mic such as AirPods no longer trips it on clean speech, and real babble now does.
  • Holding the dictation key no longer starts a second dictation right after the first one ends.
  • In an app Myna cannot type into, such as the VSCodium snap, Myna now says “No text field focused” instead of starting and stopping a second later (#91).
  • Setting up Myna retries once when the Snap Store times out, instead of reporting that Myna failed.
  • New translations: Swedish, Hungarian and Simplified Chinese; updates to Esperanto, Estonian, French and Slovak.

Thanks

For the translation work,

  • On Hosted Weblate: Balázs Úr (Hungarian), Daniel Nylander (Swedish), David D. (French), Nova_Chen and tianhe-team (Simplified Chinese), Peter Vančo (Slovak), phlostically (Esperanto) and Priit Jõerüüt (Estonian).

Install

On Ubuntu 24.04 LTS or later, install Myna Settings from the PPA:

sudo add-apt-repository ppa:canonical-desktop-team/myna
sudo apt install myna-config

Myna Settings then sets up the rest: the Dictation app and a speech model. They come from the Snap Store’s latest/edge channel as myna, myna-parakeet, myna-whisper, myna-funasr and myna-nemotron.

Myna works on GNOME, Xfce and KDE Plasma 6.

arm64 is experimental: the speech models run on the CPU, and Parakeet’s NVIDIA GPU engine is built for arm64 but has not been tried on hardware yet.

releases.title: Myna 0.3.1
releases.body:
Highlights

  • Teach Myna your words. Add names and terms to the vocabulary in Myna Settings’ Model tab, and the Parakeet model listens for them: a word it used to misspell, or split (“pulse audio” for PulseAudio), is far more likely to come out the way you wrote it (#1).
  • Whisper and FunASR do not use the vocabulary yet, and its row is hidden while one of them is the active model.
  • Switching engine or model no longer leaves the old one’s files on disk (#61).
  • Typing on Plasma Wayland keeps your keyboard layout during a dictation (#4).
  • Setting up Myna on Xfce and Plasma no longer stops at the indicator step until the next login (#79).
  • On Plasma with software rendering, the first dictation no longer stalls while the pill starts.

Known issues

  • A word that sounds exactly like a common one can still come out as the common word: “Myna” is heard as “minor” or “miner” in some accents.
  • Upgrading waits for your next logout: the running pill holds back the snap refresh (#38). The fix is waiting on the Snap Store.

Install

On Ubuntu 24.04 LTS or later, install Myna Settings from the PPA:

sudo add-apt-repository ppa:canonical-desktop-team/myna
sudo apt install myna-config

Myna Settings then sets up the rest: the Dictation app and a speech model. They come from the Snap Store’s latest/edge channel as myna, myna-parakeet, myna-whisper and myna-funasr.

Myna works on GNOME, Xfce and KDE Plasma 6.

arm64 is experimental: the speech models run on the CPU, and Parakeet’s NVIDIA GPU engine is built for arm64 but has not been tried on hardware yet.

commits.author: Robert Ancell
commits.message:
ci: automate releases and publishing to pub.dev (#77)

## Summary

Automates releases and publishing to pub.dev from GitHub Actions,
replacing the manual `chore: release` commit + `dart pub publish` flow.

### Flow

1. Conventional commits land on `main`.
2. `release.yml` (release-please) opens/updates a `chore: release X.Y.Z`
PR that bumps `pubspec.yaml` and `CHANGELOG.md`.
3. Merging that PR creates the `vX.Y.Z` tag + GitHub release, then
dispatches `publish.yml` on the tag (tags created with `GITHUB_TOKEN`
don't trigger `push` workflows).
4. `publish.yml` verifies the tag matches `pubspec.yaml`, runs analyze +
tests, then publishes via `dart-lang/setup-dart`'s reusable workflow
using OIDC (no secrets). It also runs on a manually pushed `vX.Y.Z` tag.

### Changes

- `.github/workflows/release.yml`: release-please + dispatch of publish.
- `.github/workflows/publish.yml`: verify + publish (`push` tags and
`workflow_dispatch`).
- `.github/workflows/publish-dry-run.yml`: `dart pub publish --dry-run`
on PRs.
- `.github/workflows/semantic-pr.yml`: enforces conventional PR titles.
- `release-please-config.json` / `.release-please-manifest.json`: `dart`
release type, `v` tags, pre-1.0 `feat` -> patch bump, bootstrapped at
`0.6.0` so the next release only includes new commits.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: documents the release process.


Resolves UDENG-12254

commits.message:
Rebase to core26 (#175)

Rebase the snap to core26 (2604 content):

- base: core24 -> core26

Part of the 26.04 desktop snap core26 migration (NovaLake enablement
needs mesa-2604 >= 26.2.3): on core26 the [gnome] extension auto-wires
gnome-core26 + mesa-2604 (gpu-2604), so consumer snaps track the 2604
content snaps.

**Testing:** built with snapcraft --use-lxd (snapcraft 9.2.1),
sideloaded into an Ubuntu 26.04 VM (core26 base, mesa-2604 26.2.3 edge,
gnome-core26). Service runs.

commits.author: Chris Bainbridge
commits.message:
build against the SDK's libnotify, not the archive package

The gnome-core26-sdk ships libnotify 0.8.8 dev files and the gnome
extension prepends the SDK's pkgconfig dirs to PKG_CONFIG_PATH for
every part, so meson resolves libnotify without an archive
build-package (review). The runtime library keeps resolving through
the gnome-core26 content interface.

releases.body: Rolling developer preview, replaced by every green build on desktop/26. Signed with an individual’s registered test key; snaps are unasserted and can never be refreshed. No credentials are baked in: first boot runs the plasma-setup first-boot wizard (the KDE equivalent of GNOME’s ubuntu-desktop-init) to create the user account. See manifest.txt for the source commit and the snap versions in this image. If the image was split into *.img.zst.partNN files (GitHub’s 2GiB asset cap), reassemble first: cat ubuntu-core-desktop-kde.img.zst.part* > ubuntu-core-desktop-kde.img.zst, then verify against SHA256SUMS. Decompress with: zstd -T0 -d --sparse ubuntu-core-desktop-kde.img.zst -o pc.img (the –sparse flag is required or the output allocates the full ~20G). Boot with virt-install or qemu per README.md.

commits.author: Robert Ancell
commits.message:
ci: automate releases and publishing to pub.dev (#26)

## Summary

Automates releases and publishing to pub.dev from GitHub Actions,
replacing the manual `chore: release` commit + `dart pub publish` flow.

### Flow

1. Conventional commits land on `main`.
2. `release.yml` (release-please) opens/updates a `chore: release X.Y.Z`
PR that bumps `pubspec.yaml` and `CHANGELOG.md`.
3. Merging that PR creates the `vX.Y.Z` tag + GitHub release, then
dispatches `publish.yml` on the tag (tags created with `GITHUB_TOKEN`
don't trigger `push` workflows).
4. `publish.yml` verifies the tag matches `pubspec.yaml`, runs analyze +
tests, then publishes via `dart-lang/setup-dart`'s reusable workflow
using OIDC (no secrets). It also runs on a manually pushed `vX.Y.Z` tag.

### Changes

- `.github/workflows/release.yml`: release-please + dispatch of publish.
- `.github/workflows/publish.yml`: verify + publish (`push` tags and
`workflow_dispatch`).
- `.github/workflows/publish-dry-run.yml`: `dart pub publish --dry-run`
on PRs.
- `.github/workflows/semantic-pr.yml`: enforces conventional PR titles.
- `release-please-config.json` / `.release-please-manifest.json`: `dart`
release type, `v` tags, pre-1.0 `feat` -> patch bump, bootstrapped at
`0.5.0` so the next release only includes new commits.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: documents the release process.


Resolves UDENG-12256

releases.title: v0.17.0
releases.body:
ADSys 0.17.0, published in Ubuntu stonking on October 8, 2026.

  • New upstream release (LP: #2169827):
    • Add native certificate enrollment against AD CS over LDAP and MS-ICPR, removing the need for python3-cepces:
      • Let AD decide which certificate templates the machine may enroll
      • Bootstrap trust only against CAs adsys installed
      • Manage enrolled certificates with the new adsysctl certificate commands
      • Default fresh installs to the native backend, leaving existing installations on their current configuration
    • Add support for dynamic values in policy entries
    • Query the Global Catalog when fetching GPOs, fixing policy refresh for users belonging to groups from another domain of the forest
    • Normalize downloaded assets to Unix format, so scripts and AppArmor profiles authored on Windows are no longer rejected because of CRLF line endings or a UTF-8 BOM
    • Normalize the end of the generated sudoers file
    • Fix GDM integration issues:
      • Stop denying greeter sessions running as a dynamic user, as introduced in GDM 49
      • Seed generated dconf profiles from the matching system profile, so the greeter no longer loses its vendor defaults
    • Fix dconf policies not being applied, and user settings not being saved, for users logging in with their short name: the PAM module now uses the dconf profile name normalized by adsysd, and no longer points DCONF_PROFILE to a profile that does not exist (LP: #2107971)
    • Report dconf update failures leaving the ADSys databases missing or stale instead of treating the policies as applied, and only warn when unrelated databases fail so they cannot block logins
    • Match certificate auto-enrollment registry keys case-insensitively, so settings from GPOs storing them with a different casing are no longer silently ignored (LP: #2169074)
    • Fix GPO lookup failures when the SSSD ad_server option lists several servers, falling back to the next one if a domain controller is unreachable
    • Reject unsupported Kerberos credential cache types, such as KCM: or KEYRING:, instead of treating them as file paths or falling back to a stale ticket cache
    • Retry policy scripts the kernel still reports as busy, so they are no longer occasionally skipped
    • Fix a deadlock that could hang adsysctl service cat along with the daemon output forwarding
    • Migrate the adwatchd TUI to Bubble Tea v2
    • Bump Go version to 1.26
    • Refresh policy definition files
    • Documentation updates:
      • Added explanation of dynamic policy values
      • Added meta descriptions to documentation pages
      • Clarified language on network shares
      • Documented native certificate enrollment and its commands
      • Documented that only file-backed Kerberos caches are supported
      • Dropped packagekit-tools from the getting started tutorial
      • Fixed broken links and sitemap generation
      • Implemented new homepage structure
      • Migrated documentation tooling to Starter Pack v2
      • Removed in-docs release notes
      • Restructured certificates documentation
      • Updated configuration for the documentation URL migration
    • CI and quality of life changes not impacting package functionality:
      • Added AGENTS.md instructions
      • Allowed labeled pull requests to run the end-to-end tests
      • Got the end-to-end suite running again and made it validate the certificate backend actually under test
      • Fixed the TICS report action
      • Fixed typos and grammar errors in code comments and messages
      • Improved test stability on CI
      • Properly disable Kerberos usage in AD tests
      • Skipped the patches tests when no debian directory exists
    • Bump dependencies to latest:
      • charm.land/bubbles/v2 v2.2.1
      • charm.land/bubbletea/v2 v2.0.10
      • charm.land/lipgloss/v2 v2.0.6
      • github.com/charmbracelet/glamour v1.0.0
      • github.com/coreos/go-systemd/v22 v22.7.0
      • github.com/fatih/color v1.19.0
      • github.com/fsnotify/fsnotify v1.10.1
      • github.com/godbus/dbus/v5 v5.2.2
      • github.com/kardianos/service v1.3.0
      • github.com/maruel/natural v1.3.0
      • github.com/oiweiwei/go-msrpc v1.6.4
      • github.com/oiweiwei/gokrb5.fork/v9 v9.0.8
      • github.com/pkg/sftp v1.13.11

      • github.com/stretchr/testify v1.12.1
      • golang.org/x/crypto v0.57.0
      • golang.org/x/exp v0.0.0-20231006140011-7918f672742d
      • golang.org/x/sync v0.23.0
      • golang.org/x/sys v0.48.0
      • golang.org/x/text v0.42.0
      • google.golang.org/grpc v1.83.2
      • google.golang.org/grpc/cmd/protoc-gen-go-grpc v1.6.2
      • google.golang.org/protobuf v1.36.12

commits.author: Adrian Dombeck
commits.message:
ci: Automatically cancel in-progress workflow runs on push

If commits are pushed to the same PR in quick succession, the CI jobs
run multiple times in parallel, even though older runs are usually not
needed. This change saves some resources by automatically cancelling
in-progress workflows on new pushes to the same branch.

The implementation is directly from the example of the concurrency keyword:
https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#example-using-concurrency-and-the-default-behavior

commits.author: Carlos Nihelton
commits.message:
Deploys a systemd environment generator (#61)

[systemd-envirnoment-generator](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.environment-generator.html)

It exposes key environment variables to all systemd units:
  - WSL2_DISTRO_NAME = the instance name
- WSL2_USER_PROFILE = The Windows absolute path of the user profile
directory (e.g. C:\Users\username)

Before this change:

```text
u@DESKTOP-551PQ9O:/mnt/c/Users/User$ systemctl show-environment
LANG=C.UTF-8
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/snap/bin
```

After:

```text
u@DESKTOP-551PQ9O:/mnt/c/Users/User$ systemctl show-environment
LANG=C.UTF-8
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/snap/bin
WSL2_DISTRO_NAME=Ubuntu-26.10
WSL2_USER_PROFILE=C:/Users/User
```

All systemd units inherit those variables by default, and the generator
runs quite early, so cloud-init and wsl-pro-service are some examples of
units that can benefit from this to simplify their implementation.

commits.message:
ci: automate releases and publishing to pub.dev (#47)

## Summary

Automates releases and publishing to pub.dev from GitHub Actions,
replacing the manual `chore: release` commit + `dart pub publish` flow.

### Flow

1. Conventional commits land on `main`.
2. `release.yml` (release-please) opens/updates a `chore: release X.Y.Z`
PR that bumps `pubspec.yaml` and `CHANGELOG.md`.
3. Merging that PR creates the `vX.Y.Z` tag + GitHub release, then

commits.author: Robert Ancell
commits.message:
ci: automate releases and publishing to pub.dev (#413)

## Summary

Automates releases and publishing to pub.dev from GitHub Actions,
replacing the manual `chore: release` commit + `dart pub publish` flow.

### Flow

1. Conventional commits land on `main`.
2. `release.yml` (release-please) opens/updates a `chore: release X.Y.Z`
PR that bumps `pubspec.yaml` and `CHANGELOG.md`.
3. Merging that PR creates the `vX.Y.Z` tag + GitHub release, then
dispatches `publish.yml` on the tag (tags created with `GITHUB_TOKEN`
don't trigger `push` workflows).
4. `publish.yml` verifies the tag matches `pubspec.yaml`, runs analyze +
tests, then publishes via `dart-lang/setup-dart`'s reusable workflow
using OIDC (no secrets). It also runs on a manually pushed `vX.Y.Z` tag.

### Changes

- `.github/workflows/release.yml`: release-please + dispatch of publish.
- `.github/workflows/publish.yml`: verify + publish (`push` tags and
`workflow_dispatch`).
- `.github/workflows/publish-dry-run.yml`: `dart pub publish --dry-run`
on PRs.
- `.github/workflows/semantic-pr.yml`: enforces conventional PR titles.
- `release-please-config.json` / `.release-please-manifest.json`: `dart`
release type, `v` tags, pre-1.0 `feat` -> patch bump, bootstrapped at
`0.8.1` so the next release only includes new commits.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: documents the release process.

Resolves UDENG-12242

commits.author: Kat
commits.message:
feat(gh-actions/go): New action to bump toolchain patch version (#150)

Added a new composite GH action to open PRs and update Go toolchain
directive patch versions. This works with both `go.work` and `go.mod`
files.

Generally, we want to always use the latest Go toolchain patch version
where possible, as security fixes are often tied to it. This new action
aims to simplify this process by scanning for places where the toolchain
directive is used, and open PRs to update the patch version to the
latest version when needed.

Note: we **only touch the patch version**.

By default, we ignore files in `*/vendor/*`, `*/testdata/*`, and
`*/.git/*` based on `find`'s parsing/searching.

commits.author: kkuo
commits.message:
feat(gh-actions/go): New action to bump toolchain patch version

Added a new composite GH action to open PRs and update Go toolchain directive patch versions. This works with both `go.work` and `go.mod` files.

Generally, we want to always use the latest Go toolchain patch version where possible as security fixes are often tied to it. This new action aims to simplify this process by scanning for places where the toolchain directive is used, and open PRs to update the patch version to the latest version when needed.

Note, we only ever touch the patch version.

By default, we ignore files in `*/vendor/*`, `*/testdata/*`, and `*/.git/*` based on `find`'s, parsing/searching.

commits.author: Robert Ancell
commits.message:
ci: automate releases and publishing to pub.dev (#33)

## Summary

Automates releases and publishing to pub.dev from GitHub Actions,
replacing the manual `chore: release` commit + `dart pub publish` flow.

### Flow

1. Conventional commits land on `main`.
2. `release.yml` (release-please) opens/updates a `chore: release X.Y.Z`
PR that bumps `pubspec.yaml` and `CHANGELOG.md`.
3. Merging that PR creates the `vX.Y.Z` tag + GitHub release, then
dispatches `publish.yml` on the tag (tags created with `GITHUB_TOKEN`
don't trigger `push` workflows).
4. `publish.yml` verifies the tag matches `pubspec.yaml`, runs analyze +
tests, then publishes via `dart-lang/setup-dart`'s reusable workflow
using OIDC (no secrets). It also runs on a manually pushed `vX.Y.Z` tag.

### Changes

- `.github/workflows/release.yml`: release-please + dispatch of publish.
- `.github/workflows/publish.yml`: verify + publish (`push` tags and
`workflow_dispatch`).
- `.github/workflows/publish-dry-run.yml`: `dart pub publish --dry-run`
on PRs.
- `.github/workflows/semantic-pr.yml`: enforces conventional PR titles.
- `release-please-config.json` / `.release-please-manifest.json`: `dart`
release type, `v` tags, pre-1.0 `feat` -> patch bump, bootstrapped at
`0.2.2` so the next release only includes new commits.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: documents the release process.


Resolves UDENG-12253

releases.title: Myna 0.3.3
releases.body:
Highlights

  • Hindi dictation. A new model, IndicConformer (AI4Bharat), installs as the myna-indicconformer snap, and Myna Settings recommends it for Hindi and sets it up on a Hindi desktop. On the FLEURS Hindi test set it writes 12% of words wrong, against 31% for Whisper large-v3-turbo on a GPU, the best Myna offered for Hindi until now, and it runs on the CPU, finishing about 0.15 s after you stop speaking (#82).
  • Text that Myna could not type, because focus left the field while it was still finishing, is now reported as lost instead of disappearing silently.
  • Fixes in how Myna types through IBus, including a memory bug in the preedit text it shows while you speak (#18).
  • New Azerbaijani translation; updates to Esperanto, French and Simplified Chinese.
  • Myna Settings from the retired ppa:charles05/myna-config now gets updates again: upgrading moves the system to ppa:canonical-desktop-team/myna (#111).

Thanks

  • anilsapkota, for the Hindi evaluation that made the case for IndicConformer (#82).

For the translation work,

  • On Hosted Weblate: David D. (French), Nicat (Azerbaijani), Nova_Chen (Simplified Chinese) and phlostically (Esperanto).

Install

On Ubuntu 24.04 LTS or later, install Myna Settings from the PPA:

sudo add-apt-repository ppa:canonical-desktop-team/myna
sudo apt install myna-config

Myna Settings then sets up the rest: the Dictation app and a speech model. They come from the Snap Store’s latest/edge channel as myna, myna-parakeet, myna-whisper, myna-funasr and myna-nemotron.

Myna works on GNOME, Xfce and KDE Plasma 6.

arm64 is experimental: the speech models run on the CPU, and Parakeet’s NVIDIA GPU engine is built for arm64 but has not been tried on hardware yet.

releases.title: Myna 0.3.2
releases.body:
Highlights

  • Vocabulary now works with every model. Whisper and FunASR join Parakeet in writing your names and terms the way you typed them, and each correction is checked against the audio first, so ordinary words stay as spoken. The word list moved to Myna Settings’ General tab (#1). The check has a cost on Whisper: with 100 words in the list, Whisper small takes about 0.44 s longer (median) to finish a phrase, 0.16 s with 10 words.
  • Parakeet transcribes faster: a 0.3.1 bug re-ran the decode over and over when the vocabulary was empty, making it 2.7x slower on average and more on long phrases.
  • Myna Settings’ Diagnostics shows how noisy your last dictation was (signal-to-noise ratio), and the background-noise warning now looks at that instead of at loudness, so a hot mic such as AirPods no longer trips it on clean speech, and real babble now does.
  • Holding the dictation key no longer starts a second dictation right after the first one ends.
  • In an app Myna cannot type into, such as the VSCodium snap, Myna now says “No text field focused” instead of starting and stopping a second later (#91).
  • Setting up Myna retries once when the Snap Store times out, instead of reporting that Myna failed.
  • New translations: Swedish, Hungarian and Simplified Chinese; updates to Esperanto, Estonian, French and Slovak.

Thanks

For the translation work,

  • On Hosted Weblate: Balázs Úr (Hungarian), Daniel Nylander (Swedish), David D. (French), Nova_Chen and tianhe-team (Simplified Chinese), Peter Vančo (Slovak), phlostically (Esperanto) and Priit Jõerüüt (Estonian).

Install

On Ubuntu 24.04 LTS or later, install Myna Settings from the PPA:

sudo add-apt-repository ppa:canonical-desktop-team/myna
sudo apt install myna-config

Myna Settings then sets up the rest: the Dictation app and a speech model. They come from the Snap Store’s latest/edge channel as myna, myna-parakeet, myna-whisper, myna-funasr and myna-nemotron.

Myna works on GNOME, Xfce and KDE Plasma 6.

arm64 is experimental: the speech models run on the CPU, and Parakeet’s NVIDIA GPU engine is built for arm64 but has not been tried on hardware yet.

releases.title: Myna 0.3.1
releases.body:
Highlights

  • Teach Myna your words. Add names and terms to the vocabulary in Myna Settings’ Model tab, and the Parakeet model listens for them: a word it used to misspell, or split (“pulse audio” for PulseAudio), is far more likely to come out the way you wrote it (#1).
  • Whisper and FunASR do not use the vocabulary yet, and its row is hidden while one of them is the active model.
  • Switching engine or model no longer leaves the old one’s files on disk (#61).
  • Typing on Plasma Wayland keeps your keyboard layout during a dictation (#4).
  • Setting up Myna on Xfce and Plasma no longer stops at the indicator step until the next login (#79).
  • On Plasma with software rendering, the first dictation no longer stalls while the pill starts.

Known issues

  • A word that sounds exactly like a common one can still come out as the common word: “Myna” is heard as “minor” or “miner” in some accents.
  • Upgrading waits for your next logout: the running pill holds back the snap refresh (#38). The fix is waiting on the Snap Store.

Install

On Ubuntu 24.04 LTS or later, install Myna Settings from the PPA:

sudo add-apt-repository ppa:canonical-desktop-team/myna
sudo apt install myna-config

Myna Settings then sets up the rest: the Dictation app and a speech model. They come from the Snap Store’s latest/edge channel as myna, myna-parakeet, myna-whisper and myna-funasr.

Myna works on GNOME, Xfce and KDE Plasma 6.

arm64 is experimental: the speech models run on the CPU, and Parakeet’s NVIDIA GPU engine is built for arm64 but has not been tried on hardware yet.

commits.author: Robert Ancell
commits.message:
ci: automate releases and publishing to pub.dev (#77)

## Summary

Automates releases and publishing to pub.dev from GitHub Actions,
replacing the manual `chore: release` commit + `dart pub publish` flow.

### Flow

1. Conventional commits land on `main`.
2. `release.yml` (release-please) opens/updates a `chore: release X.Y.Z`
PR that bumps `pubspec.yaml` and `CHANGELOG.md`.
3. Merging that PR creates the `vX.Y.Z` tag + GitHub release, then
dispatches `publish.yml` on the tag (tags created with `GITHUB_TOKEN`
don't trigger `push` workflows).
4. `publish.yml` verifies the tag matches `pubspec.yaml`, runs analyze +
tests, then publishes via `dart-lang/setup-dart`'s reusable workflow
using OIDC (no secrets). It also runs on a manually pushed `vX.Y.Z` tag.

### Changes

- `.github/workflows/release.yml`: release-please + dispatch of publish.
- `.github/workflows/publish.yml`: verify + publish (`push` tags and
`workflow_dispatch`).
- `.github/workflows/publish-dry-run.yml`: `dart pub publish --dry-run`
on PRs.
- `.github/workflows/semantic-pr.yml`: enforces conventional PR titles.
- `release-please-config.json` / `.release-please-manifest.json`: `dart`
release type, `v` tags, pre-1.0 `feat` -> patch bump, bootstrapped at
`0.6.0` so the next release only includes new commits.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: documents the release process.


Resolves UDENG-12254

commits.message:
e2e: Log page state when the browser login times out (#2216)

When the e2e browser login times out, the log does not show what the
page displayed. A wrong page, a slow load, and an unexpected UI change
all look the same.

On every `wait_for_pattern` timeout, log the page URI, title, load
progress, and the full visible text. The full text is logged because the
useful message can sit lower on the page.

The helper runs only on failure and swallows its own errors, so the
timeout result does not change.

Validated with a forced timeout in a GTK/WebKit window under Xvfb: the
log line prints with the full text, and the success path is unchanged.

releases.title: Ubuntu Core Desktop 26 KDE (dangerous) - 20261127
releases.body: Rolling developer preview, replaced by every green build on desktop/26. Signed with an individual’s registered test key; snaps are unasserted and can never be refreshed. No credentials are baked in: first boot runs the plasma-setup first-boot wizard (the KDE equivalent of GNOME’s ubuntu-desktop-init) to create the user account. See manifest.txt for the source commit and the snap versions in this image. If the image was split into *.img.zst.partNN files (GitHub’s 2GiB asset cap), reassemble first: cat ubuntu-core-desktop-kde.img.zst.part* > ubuntu-core-desktop-kde.img.zst, then verify against SHA256SUMS. Decompress with: zstd -T0 -d --sparse ubuntu-core-desktop-kde.img.zst -o pc.img (the –sparse flag is required or the output allocates the full ~20G). Boot with virt-install or qemu per README.md.

commits.author: Robert Ancell
commits.message:
ci: automate releases and publishing to pub.dev (#26)

## Summary

Automates releases and publishing to pub.dev from GitHub Actions,
replacing the manual `chore: release` commit + `dart pub publish` flow.

### Flow

1. Conventional commits land on `main`.
2. `release.yml` (release-please) opens/updates a `chore: release X.Y.Z`
PR that bumps `pubspec.yaml` and `CHANGELOG.md`.
3. Merging that PR creates the `vX.Y.Z` tag + GitHub release, then
dispatches `publish.yml` on the tag (tags created with `GITHUB_TOKEN`
don't trigger `push` workflows).
4. `publish.yml` verifies the tag matches `pubspec.yaml`, runs analyze +
tests, then publishes via `dart-lang/setup-dart`'s reusable workflow
using OIDC (no secrets). It also runs on a manually pushed `vX.Y.Z` tag.

### Changes

- `.github/workflows/release.yml`: release-please + dispatch of publish.
- `.github/workflows/publish.yml`: verify + publish (`push` tags and
`workflow_dispatch`).
- `.github/workflows/publish-dry-run.yml`: `dart pub publish --dry-run`
on PRs.
- `.github/workflows/semantic-pr.yml`: enforces conventional PR titles.
- `release-please-config.json` / `.release-please-manifest.json`: `dart`
release type, `v` tags, pre-1.0 `feat` -> patch bump, bootstrapped at
`0.5.0` so the next release only includes new commits.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: documents the release process.


Resolves UDENG-12256

commits.message:
Add support for communitheme (#4)

In 18.04, Yaru theme is still called Communitheme, then the special code
for toggling among the its three variants does not work.

This change takes into account the two possible names for Yaru theme and
clean the code up.
